requirement: The `habeas` skill MUST tell agents that a project without the validation test that {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` creates is not configured for Habeas, to ask the user before running `habeas setup`, and, if setup is not completed, to do no Habeas requirements work in that project.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.cli.overview_skill.setup` has no structural obligation. It says what the `habeas` skill MUST tell agents: a project without the validation test is not configured, ask the user before running `habeas setup`, and do no Habeas requirements work if setup isn't completed. That is a content obligation on the skill's text. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation through a named interface. Any wording, section layout or file organisation that conveys those instructions would satisfy it. The `{cite}` of `requirements.cli.setup` only supplies context for naming the validation test. The skill's own `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` root is the artifact whose content is judged, so no implementation edge is needed. Whether the skill's text actually says this is a behavioral or content check, outside this structural criterion.

behavioral: The requirement has three obligations for the bundled `habeas` skill. It must say that a project without the `tests/habeas.rs` validation test is not configured. It must tell agents to ask the user before running `habeas setup`. It must tell agents to do no Habeas requirements work if setup is not completed.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_habeas_skill_asks_before_setup_and_does_no_work_without_it]` covers all three. It reads the real bundled skill through `skill_md` and `workflow_steps`. It takes workflow step 1 with `step("habeas", 1)` and uses `assert_text` to require two phrases in it:

- "If Habeas is not configured yet (no `tests/habeas.rs` calling `habeas::validate()`), ask the user before running `habeas setup`". This covers the not-configured condition, which is tied to the missing validation test, and the ask-first rule.
- "if setup is not completed, do no Habeas requirements work in the project". This covers the no-work fallback.

`assert_text` asserts `text.contains(phrase)` for each phrase and fails with a message if one is missing. So a skill that dropped or changed any of the three instructions would fail the test.

The requirement only governs the skill's text, so no further behavior needs a test. Behavior of `habeas setup` itself belongs to the cited `requirements.cli.setup`, which is context here and not reassessed.

text: The `habeas` skill MUST tell agents that a project without the validation test that {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` creates is not configured for Habeas, to ask the user before running `habeas setup`, and, if setup is not completed, to do no Habeas requirements work in that project.

Running `habeas setup` in an existing Cargo and mdBook project MUST add Habeas as a dev dependency, configure `habeas mdbook` as its preprocessor, add the badge stylesheet, enable sidebar folding with `output.html.fold.enable` unless the book already sets it, and create `tests/habeas.rs` that calls `habeas::validate()`. Repeating setup MUST avoid duplicate configuration and preserve customized tests and stylesheets. Setup MUST NOT install or modify agent skills.
